summary: Mina's hills and mines: the Delvings, iron for Sonargur or Parim, the hill wardens, a seat in the Compact or Mina's own counsel, and the hills at war.

lords_of_the_delvings.name: Lords of the Delvings
lords_of_the_delvings.desc: The lords of Mina hold their hills by the right of the delve: whoever can dig a mine and keep it, keeps it. The title is old, and the iron is older.

lords_of_the_delvings_2.name: The Reeves' Law
lords_of_the_delvings_2.desc: The reeves have written the law of the mines on a roll of hide, and the lords have sworn to keep it. A quarrel over a vein is now a matter for the moot, and not for the pick.

deep_shafts_spirit.name: Deep Shafts
deep_shafts_spirit.desc: Mina's miners have sunk shafts deeper than any in the North. The ore is richer below, and the foremen are paid by the load.

deep_shafts_2.name: The Iron Hills
deep_shafts_2.desc: The hills are riddled with galleries, cart-ways and lamp-stations, a town beneath a town. Every miner knows his way out, and the ore keeps coming.

hill_wardens_spirit.name: Hill Companies
hill_wardens_spirit.desc: Every hill village keeps a company of wardens who know the paths, the passes and the places where an enemy cannot see. They do not leave the hills lightly.

hill_wardens_2.name: Wardens of the Hills
hill_wardens_2.desc: The hill companies are drilled together under the reeves' banner. They dig in swiftly, hold their ground and bleed whoever tries to move them.

hill_road_pact.name: The Hill Road Pact
hill_road_pact.desc: Mina and The Hold keep their hill roads open to each other's carts, and charge no toll. Their merchants have a saying about tolls that is not repeatable.

own_counsel_mina.name: Mina Keeps Its Name
own_counsel_mina.desc: Mina sells its iron to Sonargur, and takes its counsel from nobody. The moot has said so, and the reeves have sealed it.

shared_watch.name: The Watch Shared
shared_watch.desc: The hill-beacons of Mina are lit in time with the beacons of its neighbours, and the signals are the same. A warning passed along the hills reaches Sonargur in an hour.

hills_arm.name: The Hills Arm
hills_arm.desc: The hills have taken up the sword. Smelters work through the night, wardens man every pass, and the whole of Mina is ready to answer the horn.

chapel_in_the_hills.title: A Chapel in the Hills
chapel_in_the_hills.desc: The almoners of the Houses of the First Light have come to the hill villages with a plan: a chapel and a hall of healing, a granary and a register of births. The reeves of Mina are wary of anyone who builds on their hills without paying for the stone.

iron_contract.title: Iron from Mina
iron_contract.desc: A smelt-master of Mina has come with a string of carts loaded with bar-iron and a contract. Lord Etonar offers a year's supply at a good price, to be paid in advance and delivered to the river. The offer is fair, and he is not the only one who has made it.

mina_envoys.title: Envoys from Mina
mina_envoys.desc: Envoys from the hills of Mina have come to The Hold with an offer: to keep the hill roads open between the two lands, toll-free, for a thousand years. They bring a map and a sample of the road-stone.

focuses.name: The Lord of Mina
focuses.desc: Lord Etonar governs four states of hills and mines through a moot of reeves and smelt-masters. The iron of Mina goes down the river to Sonargur, and the silver comes back up.

focuses.name: The Hill Moot
focuses.desc: The moot of reeves meets in a cavern under the hill, where the voices carry and the lamps never go out. Etonar sits on a stone chair at its head.

focuses.name: Chapels in the Hills
focuses.desc: The almoners ask to raise chapels in the hill villages. The reeves are not sure, and the miners are rather keen.

focuses.name: The Reeves' Law
focuses.desc: The reeves write the law of the mines: how a vein is claimed, how a shaft is shared and what a miner is owed for a lost hand.

focuses.name: Ledgers of Iron
focuses.desc: Every shaft has a clerk and every cart has a tally. At the end of the quarter, the moot knows to the pound what the hills have yielded.

focuses.name: Mina United
focuses.desc: Lords, reeves and smelt-masters take one oath on the hill-stone. The banner of Mina, a hammer on a grey field, is raised over every mine.

focuses.name: The Delvings
focuses.desc: The Delvings of Mina are shafts and galleries cut into the hills in an age no one remembers. New pits are sunk beside the old, and the lamps are trimmed.

focuses.name: Deep Shafts
focuses.desc: The miners go deeper, and the ore is richer for it. Pumps are installed, ladders are replaced by cages and the foremen are paid by the load.

focuses.name: River Barges
focuses.desc: Barges carry the iron from the hill-heads to the river towns. The locks are rebuilt and the towpaths widened, and the bargemen are paid in advance.

focuses.name: Smelting Halls
focuses.desc: Great halls with a dozen furnaces each are raised at the hill-foot. The fires are never let out, and the glow can be seen from the next valley.

focuses.name: Iron for Sonargur
focuses.desc: Mina signs a yearly contract to send iron to the crown at Sonargur. The price is fair, the carts are regular and the reeves hold the key.

focuses.name: Iron for Parim
focuses.desc: Parim pays well for iron, and Mina has never refused a good price. A contract is drawn up with the king's factors, and the carts head south.

focuses.name: The Quarries of Mina
focuses.desc: Grey stone for walls and good white stone for halls are cut from the hills in great blocks. They are carted away to build, and the pits are left to fill with water.

focuses.name: The Iron Hills
focuses.desc: The hills of Mina are known across the North for their iron. Miners and smelters take a pride in the name, and the iron lives up to it.

focuses.name: Hill Wardens
focuses.desc: Every pass has its warden and every village its spear. Etonar names a captain for each of the hill-roads and orders them to drill in the autumn.

focuses.name: Hill Companies
focuses.desc: The wardens are formed into companies, each from a single valley, each led by a reeve. They know the hills better than the hills know themselves.

focuses.name: Pikes of Mina Iron
focuses.desc: The smelters of Mina forge long pike-heads and broad shield-bosses from their best iron. The wardens carry them with a pride that comes of knowing where the iron came from.

focuses.name: Forts in the Passes
focuses.desc: Stone forts are raised in the narrowest passes, with a wall, a well and a store of arrows. Anyone who comes through the hills comes through a gate.

focuses.name: The Mina Levy
focuses.desc: The moot orders a levy from every hill village. The miners go to the muster with their picks over their shoulders, and are given spears when they arrive.

focuses.name: Wardens of the Hills
focuses.desc: The hill companies are drilled together under the reeves' banner, and learn to dig in as fast as a mine-gang. Whoever meets them in the passes will pay for every foot.

focuses.name: Sonargur's Friend
focuses.desc: Mina leans toward Sonargur because Sonargur buys its iron. The moot makes the leaning official, and writes a letter to the crown.

focuses.name: Envoys to The Hold
focuses.desc: Mina is friends with its neighbour The Hold, and sends envoys to say so. They carry samples of iron, a map of the hill roads and a proposal.

focuses.name: A Seat in the Compact
focuses.desc: Mina asks Lerendor for a seat in the Leren Compact. The Compact buys Mina's iron already; a seat would make the arrangement a lasting one.

focuses.name: The Hill Road Pact
focuses.desc: The pact is cut in a stone and set at the border: the hill roads are open to both lands, and no toll is charged on either side.

focuses.name: Compact Iron
focuses.desc: Mina's iron arms the Compact, and Mina is among its first customers. The smelters are given a contract, and the carts are given priority at the river locks.

focuses.name: Mina Keeps Its Name
focuses.desc: The moot decides that Mina sells iron to anyone who pays and joins nobody's alliance. The reeves put it on a stone, in the cavern where the moot meets.

focuses.name: The Watch Shared
focuses.desc: The beacons of the hills are lit in time with the beacons of Mina's neighbours. A warning in the passes is known in Sonargur within the hour.

focuses.name: The Hills Arm
focuses.desc: The beacons are lit on every peak, and the wardens are called to their passes. The Lord of Mina says that the hills have taken up the sword.

focuses.name: Iron for the Watch
focuses.desc: The smelters work day and night to arm the northern watch. Cart after cart of spear-heads and shield-bosses rolls down to the river.

focuses.name: Hold the Hills
focuses.desc: The passes are barred with stone and timber, and the forts are manned from end to end. Whoever comes over the hills must come through them.

focuses.name: Miners with the Heir
focuses.desc: The Heir has returned, and the miners of Mina volunteer to dig him a road. They bring picks and spades, and the wardens come with spears.

focuses.name: The Delvings Reopen
focuses.desc: The beacon-fires burn low and the shafts are opened once more. The wardens go home with their wages, and the miners go back to the pits.
